newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Lawyer says PLO's Arafat ordered journalist held.
newsitem.headline: Lawyer says PLO's Arafat ordered journalist held.

text.p: Palestinian journalist Daoud Kuttab, held by PLO police since Wednesday, was jailed on orders from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, his brother said on Sunday.

U.S. Consul-General Edward Abington visited Kuttab, who holds American citizenship, in prison last week and Washington has called for his release, said the brother. Kuttab is on a hunger strike, demanding he either be freed or charged.

"Nobody has told us officially why he's being held but we are now told very clearly the orders to arrest him came from Yasser Arafat," lawyer Jonathan Kuttab, who is acting as his brother's attorney, told Reuters.
He said the information came from police colonel Faris al-Amleh of Ramallah, where Kuttab is being held, adding that police had prevented him and others from visiting Kuttab since Thursday.

He said the detention was apparently related to a dispute between Kuttab, who has a private contract to carry live transmissions of Palestinian Legislative Council sessions, and Arafat's Palestinian Authority which may not want the sessions broadcast live.
"These sessions are very open, very democratic and frank and sometimes very critical of the Palestinian Authority," said Kuttab.
A Western diplomat said Arafat refused to discuss the arrest with U.S. consulate officials who tried to contact him on the matter.
Kuttab, who lives in East Jerusalem, obeyed a summons by Palestinian police and went to the Ramallah self-rule enclave in the West Bank where he was detained.

The U.S.-based Human Rights Watch assailed the Palestinian Authority for detaining the award-winning journalist, citing a "pattern of harassment" since Arafat established his self-rule administration in parts of the West Bank and Gaza in 1994.

"This incident follows a disturbing pattern of harassment by the Palestinian Authority of journalists, human rights monitors and other government critics, a number of whom have been detained solely for exercising their internationally guaranteed right to free expression," the group said on Friday.
The United States, calling for Kuttab's release, said on Thursday that the matter had been raised with senior members of the Palestinian Authority but not directly with Arafat.
